name: Selenium
short: Excess causes selenosis: diarrhoea, fatigue, hair loss, nail changes (outbreak from a mislabelled supplement). One trial found more type 2 diabetes; a pooled analysis was not significant.
text: An outbreak of acute selenium poisoning (201 cases) was traced to a liquid supplement that contained 200 times the labelled concentration of selenium; frequently reported symptoms were diarrhoea, fatigue, hair loss, joint pain, nail discolouration or brittleness and nausea, and nail changes, fatigue and hair loss persisted for 90 days or longer in some people. In a secondary analysis of a randomised trial in 1202 people, type 2 diabetes developed more often with selenium than with placebo (hazard ratio 1.55, 95% CI 1.03 to 2.33), whereas a meta-analysis of four trials with 20,294 participants found a pooled relative risk of 1.09 that was not statistically significant. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
